body.statement: The coordinate projection of a semialgebraic set defined over the real algebraic numbers is semialgebraic over the real algebraic numbers.  Every finite family of semialgebraic subsets of \(\mathbb R^d\) admits a finite compatible smooth semialgebraic stratification.  Every semialgebraic set has finitely many connected components, and each connected component can be joined by a semialgebraic path that is piecewise continuously differentiable.

source.locator: Theorem 2.2.1, Theorem 2.4.5, Proposition 2.5.13, and Chapter 9, Section 9.1
source.verbatim_statement: Open-source restatements explicitly attributing these facts to BCR say: “Every projection of a semialgebraic set is again semialgebraic.” “Every semialgebraic set has a finite number of connected components and each such component is semialgebraic. Every connected semialgebraic set S is semialgebraically path connected.” “Then there exists a Nash stratification (Eα)α∈A for E such that each Fλ is the union of some of the strata Eα.” “Any semialgebraic curve in R^N is piecewise C^1.”

upstream.citation: J. Bochnak, M. Coste, M.-F. Roy, Real Algebraic Geometry, Springer, 1998, DOI 10.1007/978-3-662-03718-8

attestation.note: Lawful corroboration from openly accessible sources: arXiv:1709.08424 abstract (projection); Lee et al., Infima of Semialgebraic Functions, Lemma 4 (components and paths); Borowiecki, On the convergence of critical points on real algebraic sets, Theorem 20 explicitly identified as BCR Proposition 9.1.8 (compatible Nash stratification); Pleśniak, My joint research with Mirosław Baran (piecewise C1 curves). The Springer book text itself was unavailable; these exact restatements collectively cover the cited composite lemma.
